title: What pavé means and how it's set

hook.text: This ring is paved like a street.

lines.text: This ring is paved like a street.
Pavé means paved in French, with stones set close like cobblestones.
lines.say: Pavay means paved in French, with stones set close like cobblestones.

lines.text: Each stone is often a hundredth of a carat, about 1.3 mm.
lines.say: Each stone is often a hundredth of a carat, about one point three millimeters.

lines.text: A setter drills a hole and cuts a seat for every stone.
Then a graver raises small beads of metal that hold them in.
One bead often holds two neighboring stones at the same time.
Micro pavé goes down to half a millimeter, set under a microscope.
lines.say: Micro pavay goes down to half a millimeter, set under a microscope.

lines.text: Pavé caught on in Art Deco jewelry of the 1920s and 30s.
lines.say: Pavay caught on in Art Deco jewelry of the nineteen twenties and thirties.

lines.text: This render shows each of those stones with its own sparkle,
so the client sees the pavé before a single stone is set.
lines.say: so the client sees the pavay before a single stone is set.

post.youtube_title: What pavé means and how it's set
post.caption: Pavé is French for paved: small stones set close together so the metal looks paved. Each stone is often a hundredth of a carat, held by small beads of metal that a setter raises with a graver, and micro pavé goes down to half a millimeter. The renders in this video were made from the ring's 3D file with HeyGema.
